archetypes.name: reader-sweep
archetypes.rationale: The plan's highest-stated failure mode is a missed reader left at the old round_dir path; systematic enumeration of every pre-coder artifact literal is the only way to confirm completeness.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every literal occurrence of 'pre-coder-head.txt', 'pre-coder-tracked-paths.txt', and 'pre-coder-path-diffs' across all files in the scope list. For each occurrence, verify the plan accounts for it: either it appears in the list of repointed readers, or it is explicitly documented as intentionally staying at the old location. Flag any literal reference the plan omits without explanation. Also verify that the pre_coder_snapshot_dir helper is defined before its first call-site in the execution order within each script that uses it. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: grant-boundary
archetypes.rationale: The relocation's security guarantee rests on the unverified assumption that the Codex coder's --add-dir grants do not cover the new sibling snapshot directory; the plan explicitly flags this as a potential failure mode.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the actual codex dispatch invocation in the scope files to identify every --add-dir and -C/--workspace flag passed to the external coder. Confirm that the new snapshot location (a sibling of round_dir under the same IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR parent) is not reachable through any of those grants. If any grant path transitively includes the sibling directory, or if --full-auto semantics could grant broader write access than the --add-dir list implies, flag it as a plan gap requiring mitigation. Also verify that the Cursor coder path (--workspace '$PWD') cannot reach the snapshot dir given it lives outside the repo root. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
